speaker: A
text: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining the weekly product sync. Let us start with the release status.

speaker: B
text: Sure. The mobile release went out on Tuesday and adoption is around forty percent so far.

speaker: A
text: Forty percent in three days is better than last quarter. Any crash reports worth escalating?

speaker: C
text: We saw a spike on Android fourteen devices, mostly around the camera permission dialog.

speaker: B
text: That matches the support tickets. Roughly thirty users reported the same freeze yesterday.

speaker: A
text: Alright, let us treat that as a blocker for the next patch. Who can own the investigation?

speaker: C
text: I can take it. I already have a reproduction on a physical Pixel device in the lab.

speaker: B
text: I will pair with you in the afternoon. I have the logs from the failing sessions.

speaker: A
text: Great. Next topic, the pricing experiment. What did the first week of data show us?

speaker: B
text: Conversion on the annual plan went up by six percent, but monthly churn also went up slightly.

speaker: C
text: The churn increase may be seasonal. Last year we saw the same pattern in September.

speaker: A
text: Can we isolate the seasonal effect before we commit to rolling this out globally?

speaker: B
text: Yes, I will run the analysis against last year cohorts and share it on Thursday.

speaker: A
text: Perfect. Third topic, hiring. We still have two open roles on the platform team.

speaker: C
text: I screened four candidates this week. Two of them are moving to the technical interview.

speaker: B
text: Do we have enough interviewers? Last round we had to reschedule twice because of conflicts.

speaker: A
text: I will ask the infrastructure team to lend us two interviewers for the next two weeks.

speaker: C
text: That would help a lot. The candidates were frustrated by the long gaps between rounds.

speaker: B
text: Agreed. A faster loop usually means a better acceptance rate for senior engineers.

speaker: A
text: Noted. Let us move to the documentation gap that came up in the customer review.

speaker: C
text: The onboarding guide is outdated. It still references the old settings screen from March.

speaker: B
text: I can rewrite the onboarding section if someone reviews the screenshots afterwards.

speaker: A
text: I will review them. Please keep the structure but update every screenshot and the API examples.

speaker: C
text: We should also add a troubleshooting page. Most tickets are about the same three errors.

speaker: B
text: Good idea. I will collect the top errors from the support queue and send them over.

speaker: A
text: Excellent. Last item, the quarterly planning offsite. Does the second week of October work?

speaker: C
text: The second week works for me, but I am traveling on the Monday of that week.

speaker: B
text: Tuesday to Thursday would be fine on my side. I will block the calendar now.

speaker: A
text: Let us lock Tuesday to Thursday then, and I will book the meeting room today.

speaker: C
text: Should we invite the design team for the first day, or keep it engineering only?

speaker: A
text: Invite design for the first day. The roadmap discussion needs them in the room.

speaker: B
text: I will send the invitation and prepare a short agenda before the end of the week.

speaker: A
text: Thanks everyone. To summarize, camera crash is a blocker, pricing analysis lands Thursday.

speaker: C
text: And I will own the crash investigation plus the troubleshooting documentation page.

speaker: B
text: And I will handle the onboarding rewrite, the cohort analysis, and the offsite agenda.

speaker: A
text: That is everything. Let us end a few minutes early today. Talk to you tomorrow.
